To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Jatropha biodiesels are being promoted by the Indian government to reduce dependence on foreign oil, improve the livelihoods of farmers and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
Jatropha biodiesels are being promoted as a solution to multiple policy challenges in India.

(1) Jatropha plantations are displacing traditional land use activities in Jhadol tehsil, Rajasthan; (2) the displaced activities are of particular importance to the poorest households in the study area; (3) the displaced land use activities provide important livelihood benefits to the poorest households; and (4) these livelihood benefits are being lost as a result of the displacement of traditional land uses by Jatropha plantings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: 1) The potential land use implications for the Indian Jatropha biodiesal programme.
understanding the social and environmental consequences of biofuel development in India.
the unconsidered impacts on local land-use systems and livelihoods of the rapid expansion of Jatropha plantations in Rajasthan, India for biodiesel production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Jatropha is not a panacea for the rural poor, and that its development needs to be carefully managed.
the Jatropha biodiesal program in Jhadol, Rajasthan, has not benefited the poor, and in some cases has made their lives more difficult.
the Jatropha biodiesels are not sustainable in India and the world.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Jatropha plantations are not only displacing the traditional land use practices but also the traditional livelihoods.
the Jatropha plantations are not displacing any other crops, but are displacing the grazing land of the local pastoralist communities, who are already on the margins of poverty.
Jatropha biodiesels are not a panacea for the world's energy and climate problems, but rather a new set of problems for the poor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local impacts of biofuel production should be considered when setting policy and targets for the biofuels industry.
the impacts of Jatrophas production in India are not limited to its effects on land use, and are not necessarily positive.
the land-use impacts of biofuel production need to be understood in terms of the local land use systems that are being displaced.
